Phosphine-Catalyzed Sequential [3+3]/Aza-6 π-Electrocyclization
Reaction of Cross-Conjugated Azatrienes and δ‑Sulfonamido-
Allenoates
Ning Li and You Huang *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 9392 −9397 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: An unprecedented sequential [3+3]/aza-6 π-electrocyclization between cross-conjugated azatrienes and δ-
sulfonamido-allenoates, catalyzed by phosphine, has been developed, which provides e ﬃcient and facile access to highly
functionalized tetrahydroisoquinoline derivatives. The products can be easily transformed into (dihydro)isoquinolines and their
fused polycyclic compounds. The reactivity of both azatrienes and δ-sulfonamido-allenoates in this text, acting as a ﬁve-atom unit, is
unique in the phosphine-catalyzed annulations of allenoates.
F
or decades, methodologies developed by phosphine-
catalyzed reactions, especially those between allenoates
and various electrophiles, have become a powerful and facile
tool for the construction of complex structures. 1 However, the
explosive development of phosphine catalysis has been greatly
impeded in the past two years most likely due to the “old-
patterned” reaction modes and synthons. 2 Our group has been
dedicated to the exploration of phosphine catalysis, aiming at
not only valuable skeletons formed in new reactions 3 but also
the discovery of brand-new allenoates 4 that may act as totally
diﬀerent building blocks and lead to novel reaction modes,
which, in our opinion, may reveal a promising breakthrough for
the development of phosphine catalysis in the future.
Inspired by the unique “trinucleophilic site ” mode of the δ-
sulfonamido-allenoate developed in our previous work, 4a we
envisioned that more interesting chemistry could be developed
with this novel allenoate. Cross-conjugated heterotrienes, as
the heterosubstituted derivatives of dendralenes, captured our
attention. Due to their unique ability to undergo sequential
addition reactions, dendralenes are versatile building blocks for
the quick generation of complex structures. 5 For instance, a
cross-conjugated oxatriene was found to be a readily available
Michael acceptor that is prone to undergo two additions. In
2011, Yan and co-workers disclosed an e ﬃcient synthesis of
optically active cyclohexanones through asymmetric organo-
catalytic double-conjugate addition of malononitrile.
6 Sim-
ilarly, when a wide variety of nucleophilic reagents were
adopted, cascade additions occurred and provided diverse
cyclic compounds through [5+1] annulations ( Scheme 1, a).7,8
In addition, dibenzylidene acetone was also able to participate
in the [3+2] 9 and [4+2]10 reactions with allenoates or electron
deﬁcient oleﬁns under organocatalysis ( Scheme 1, b and c, X =

O). On the contrary, there have been few reports about cross-
conjugated azatrienes. In general, cross-conjugated azatrienes
bearing an electron-withdrawing sulfonyl or benzoyl group on
the nitrogen atom underwent, on heating or in the presence of
amine catalysts, an inverse electron demand hetero-Diels −
Alder reaction with electron-rich dienophiles or aldehydes
(Scheme 1 ,c ,X=N R ′).
11,12 Chi and co-workers reported a
DMAP-catalyzed reaction of α-chloro acetic ester that
provided attractive access to pyridines. 12b Apart from that,
Leung developed a palladacycle-catalyzed addition of Ph 2PH
to α,β-unsaturated imines while there was one case of
azatrienes involved. 13 Among all of these cases, only single-
ring compounds were formed on the basis of a desymmetriza-
tion strategy via simple addition reactions, while the potential
of cross-conjugated azatrienes to undergo sequential annula-
tion to construct valuable fused-ring products remains
challenging.
By employing novel δ-sulfonamido-allenoates, we hypothe-
sized that cross-conjugated heterotrienes would undergo a rare
[3+3] annulation, and the intermediate formed will be
involved in an intramolecular aza-6 π-electrocyclization, a ﬀord-
ing a bicyclic skeleton in one step. To the best of our
knowledge, there has no report about aza-6 π-electrocyclization
involved in the annulation between allenoates and electrophiles
catalyzed by phosphine. Herein, we developed the ﬁrst
sequential [3+3]/aza-6 π-electrocyclization reaction that o ﬀers
a general method for the e ﬃcient construction of polysub-
stituted hydroisoquinolines ( Scheme 1 , d). Moreover, the
products could be easily transformed into aromatic bicyclic
rings. Hydroisoquinoline and isoquinoline derivatives are
frequently found in pharmaceuticals and bioactive natural
products, as well as organocatalysts ( Figure 1 ).
14−18 For
example, Ambelline15 and pancratistatin16 are known to exhibit
pronounced cytostatic activity. Roxadustat 18 (also known as
FG-4592) is an orally bioavailable hypoxia-inducible factor
(HIF) prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor that promotes coordinated
erythropoiesis.
Initially, we started the approach by employing δ-
sulfonamido-allenoate 2b and cross-conjugated azatriene 1a
or dibenzylidene acetone (dba) 4 in the presence of PCy
3 and
K2CO3 (for optimization of the reaction conditions, see Table
S1). Gratifyingly, the reaction between 1a and 2b in
chloroform delivered the desired product 3ab in 24% yield
with a diastereomeric ratio (dr) of 10: l. After conditions had
been screened, the use of P(4-MeC
6H4)3 (20 mol %) with
K3PO4·3H2O (50 mol %) as a base in 1 mL of dichloro-
methane at 60 °C (sealed tube immersed in an oil bath)
proved to be optimal.
With the optimized condition in hand, we then turned to
explore the generality of this novel strategy for the construction
of highly substituted hydroisoquinolines. At ﬁrst, we set out to
investigate the scope of cross-conjugated azatrienes. Substrates
1a−1h bearing an electron-donating group (Me and OMe) or
an electron-withdrawing group (CF
3 and CN) as well as a
halide (F, Cl, and Br) at the para position of both phenyl rings
led to 3aa−3ha in good yields with dr ranging from 4.8:1 to
8.3:1 ( Scheme 2 ). The structure and relative con ﬁguration of
the major isomer ( anti) were con ﬁrmed by X-ray crystallo-
graphic analysis ( 3fa, CCDC 2012531).20 Similarly, the
reaction between δ-sulfonamido-allenoate 2a and cross
conjugated aza-trienes 1i−1k with di ﬀerent substituents at
the meta position of the phenyl ring went smoothly to a ﬀord
the desired hydroisoquinolines with acceptable diastereoselec-
tivity. There is no obvious electric e ﬀect observed in these
results. Surprisingly, products 3la and 3ma were well tolerated
for the reaction, even in higher yields (91% and 77%,
respectively). Moreover, it was found that azatrienes 1
containing a 2-naphthyl or heteroaryl group (thio) could also
be used in this reaction with similar results. Product 3na could
be prepared on a gram scale under the optimal condition, and
nearly 50% catalyst could be recovered. It is noteworthy that
substrates 1 with multiple substitutions on the phenyl group in
this methodology were provided with comparable yields ( 3pa−
3ta). Speci ﬁcally, product 3ra with a 3,4,5-tri-MeO sub-
stitution on both phenyl rings was not stable during
puriﬁcation on silica gel. Aryl groups with larger steric groups
were compatible with this sequential annulation; even 2,4,6-tri-
MeO-substituted substrate 1t aﬀorded the polyphenyl
tetrahydroisoquinoline derivative. When we changed the aryl
group into an aliphatic substitution (methyl for 1y), the
corresponding product was also obtained ( 3ya, 15%, eq 1 ),
which revealed the feasibility of aliphatic substituted hydro-
isoquinolines, while 1z exhibited no reactivity because of bulky
hindrance (67% recovered, eq 2).

To further expand the scope of this methodology, we then
investigated the synthesis of hydroisoquinolines with respect to
diﬀerent δ-sulfonamido-allenoates 2. As shown in Scheme 3 ,
the current reaction showed good tolerance to the aryl group
with para and meta substituents, giving 3ab−3af in moderate
to good yields. It should be noted that allenoate 2g, which had
a dichlorophenyl group, did participate in the reaction.
However, the corresponding product 3ag was obtained as a
mixture with at least three pairs of isomers because of the extra
axial chirality along with the 2,4-dichlorophenyl group.
Moreover, allenoates 2h and 2i derived from 2-naphth- and
furylaldehyde, respectively, were injected into the reaction
mixture under the optimal condition, leading to the
construction of hydroisoquinoline derivatives in moderate
yields (77% and 63%, respectively). Surprisingly, δ-nPr-
substituted sulfonamido-allenoate could also participate in
this transformation, albeit in low yield ( 3aj, 25%), while there
is no corresponding product detected for another two δ-alkyl-
substituted sulfonamido-allenoates (Cy for 2m and H for 2n).
Finally, the corresponding hydroisoquinoline derivatives with
bulky steric esters (isopropyl for 3ak and tert-butyl for 3al)
were obtained with similar results.
Following the substrate scope evaluation, we attempted to
expand the scope of azatrienes. In the presence of P(4-
MeC
6H4)3 and K 3PO4·3H2O, treatment of 4-bromobenzene
sulfonamide 3u with allenoate 2a aﬀorded annulation product
3aa in 73% yield with a dr of 8.3:1, the same ratio as that of the
reaction between substrate 1a and allenoate 2a (Scheme 4, a).
This result demonstrated that the amino group in the product
comes from δ-sulfonamido-allenoate 2a.T h er e a c t i o n s
between cross-conjugated azatrienes with asymmetric sub-
stitution on the two phenyl groups and 2a, however, did not
show good regioselectivity, and they all ended up with mess of
isomers, regardless of the di ﬀerence in the electric e ﬀect or
steric hindrance (see Scheme S1). Our endeavor to develop an
asymmetric edition of this annulation turned out to be in vain,
because all tests in the presence of chiral phosphine catalysts
resulted in racemization (see Scheme S3 ).
Then the deuterium labeling experiment was conducted to
gain insight into the reaction mechanism ( Scheme 4 , b).
1H
NMR analysis showed deuterium incorporation at position C2,
and nearly no deuterium was detected at position C1, which
may rule out other pathways to the ﬁnal product (see the
Supporting Information for details). Moreover, the result
between imine 11 and allenoate 2a also gave us a clue about
how the ﬁrst annulation reached completion.
On the basis of the results presented above and the related
literature precedent, 4a,19 a possible mechanism for this novel
reaction is depicted in Figure 2 . Intermediate A, formed
through the nucleophilic attack of the phosphine catalyst on
the β-site of δ-sulfonamido-alleno ate 2a, undergoes proton
shifts and isomerization to deliver active species B as reported
in our previous work. 4a Next, Michael addition from B to 1a or
11 results in C, which undergoes another proton shift to a ﬀord
D. Driven by the eneamine anion, an intramolecular 1,2-
addition to the imine takes place, furnishing intermediate E
through a rarely reported [3+3] process between the cross-
conjugated azatriene and allenoate. After subsequent proton
shift, the 4-methylbenzenesulfonamide anion serves as both a
leaving group and a potential base to abstract the α-site proton,
to produce I. Then, the release of the PR
3 catalyst a ﬀords
intermediate J (R′ = CH = CHPh) and K (R′ = Ph). Finally, J
undergoes an aza-6 π-electrocyclization to deliver 3aa as the
product, while the aromatization of K leads to benzannulation
product 12. In our view, the fact that no enantioselectivity
priority was observed among all of the trials may reveal the
great chance of the presence of an electrocyclization process,
due to its inherent quality (see the Supporting Information for
asymmetric attempts under chiral phosphine catalysts).

to dihydroisoquinoline 6na, which could be easily transformed
into isoquinoline derivative 7na with DDQ. Treatment with 3
equiv of DDQ of product 3na directly a ﬀorded 7na. We were
delighted to ﬁnd that fused penta- and tetracyclic molecules 9
and 10 could be readily accessible through Friedel −Crafts
acylation mediated by TfOH and lactonization mediated by
BBr
3, respectively.
In conclusion, we have developed an unprecedented
sequential annulation that provides an e ﬃcient and facile
strategy for the preparation of highly substituted tetrahy-
droisoquinolines. Reactivities of both substrates, including
cross-conjugated azatrienes and δ-sulfonamido-allenoates, were
unique and totally di ﬀerent from reported examples. Under
mild conditions, two new cycles and three bonds are formed in
a one-step process. Furthermore, products could be trans-
formed into dihydro- and isoquinolines and polyfused rings
with greatly improved molecular complexity. Mechanistic
studies may imply the presence of aza-6 π-electrocyclization
that has been rarely reported in the annulations mediated by
phosphine catalysts.
